key_insight: A feedforward neural network using the writhe density matrix can classify the first six prime two-component links with high accuracy, suggesting the matrix encodes topology-relevant structure.
engineering_relevance: This offers a fast surrogate for link classification in polymer, DNA, and protein systems where exact topological calculations can become computationally expensive.
method: Computed writhe density matrices from equilibrated link configurations
Trained a feedforward neural network on these matrix features
Tested robustness across temperature, component length, and added Gaussian noise
evidence_signal: The model achieved 97% accuracy on thermally equilibrated configurations and remained strong across temperatures and lengths, but performance dropped sharply under topology-altering Gaussian noise.
watch_item: The approach may be sensitive to noise that changes topology, so generalization to more complex or partially observed link geometries should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Writhe-Based Polymer Link Classification Using Machine Learning
